# node_modules cache scripts

Shared helpers used by the GitHub Actions workflows to store and restore the
`node_modules` cache. They exist so the archive format and compression flags
live in a single place instead of being duplicated across every workflow.

Each script takes an action argument:

| Script | Platform | `archive` | `extract` |
| ------ | -------- | --------- | --------- |
| `cache.sh <action>` | Linux / macOS | Create `node-modules-<part>.tzst` (cache miss) | Restore `node-modules*.tzst` (cache hit) |
| `cache.ps1 <action>` | Windows | Create `cache-<part>.7z` (cache miss) | Restore `cache*.7z` (cache hit) |

Linux/macOS use multi-threaded `zstd` (`node-modules-<part>.tzst`); Windows uses 7-Zip
(`cache-<part>.7z`). The archives must NOT be named `cache.tzst`: `actions/cache` names
its own tarball `cache.tzst` and passes `--exclude cache.tzst`, which would drop
our archive and save an empty cache. The two families are not interchangeable,
so the cache key already encodes the OS (`node_modules-linux-*`,
`node_modules-windows-*`, …).

One tar or 7-Zip process extracts the ~175k files of node_modules much more slowly than several in
parallel: on the Windows runners, one 7-Zip archive took 64 seconds and 8 parts 27 seconds. So
[splitList.ts](./splitList.ts) splits the list of files into 8 parts that take about as long to extract,
and the scripts archive and extract the parts in parallel. `extract` also restores the single
`node-modules.tzst` or `cache.7z` of the caches saved before the parts.

Example usage from a workflow step:

```yaml
- name: Extract node_modules cache
  if: steps.cache-node-modules.outputs.cache-hit == 'true'
  run: ./.github/workflows/node_modules_cache/cache.sh extract

- name: Create node_modules archive
  if: steps.cache-node-modules.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
  run: ./.github/workflows/node_modules_cache/cache.sh archive
```

If you change the archive format or flags, update both the `archive` and
`extract` branch of the script, and bump `build/.cachesalt` to invalidate
existing caches, unless `extract` still restores them, as it does the single
archive of the caches saved before the parts.

## Warming the caches on `main` and the release branches

Pull requests can only restore caches saved on their base branch or on `main`, so [pr-node-modules.yml](../pr-node-modules.yml) saves the node_modules, Electron, built-in extensions, WSL installer and Playwright browsers caches on every push to `main` and to the `release/*` branches. Most pushes don't change any of them, so the `Detect Missing Caches` job first computes each platform job's cache keys on a GitHub-hosted runner and lists the caches that the pushed branch can restore: its own and, on a release branch, those of `main`, which the jobs restore without saving a copy (see [detect-missing-caches](../../actions/detect-missing-caches/detect.ts)). A platform job only starts its runner when one of its caches is missing, for example after a dependency change or a cache eviction. All platform jobs run when the detection fails.

The detection mirrors the cache keys of the platform jobs, including the CRLF line endings of the Windows checkouts, and the cache versions that `actions/cache` matches in addition to the key: they depend on the cache paths, including the home directory of the runners for Electron. A cache with another version counts as missing, so the job runs and saves a compatible one; if the detection then keeps warning about a version, update its cache paths. When you change a cache key, path, key prefix, or the jobs of the workflow, update `cacheWarmingJobs` and `getCaches` in `detect.ts`; `build/lib/test/detectMissingCaches.test.ts` fails until they match.

At most one run of the workflow is in progress, and newer pushes replace its pending run, so concurrent pushes don't install the same missing dependencies several times.

## Pull requests without a cache of their dependencies

A pull request that changes the dependencies, or that runs before `pr-node-modules.yml` saved the caches of a dependency change on its base branch, has no cache of its dependencies. Installing every dependency takes about 10 minutes on Windows. Instead, [restore-node-modules](../../actions/restore-node-modules/action.yml) restores the latest cache of the same key prefix, of other dependencies, and the job's dependency installation updates it: `pnpm install` only adds, removes and builds the packages that differ.

A node_modules folder only works with the native module build configuration, Node.js and pnpm versions, pnpm settings and pnpm store location that created it, so [save-node-modules](../../actions/save-node-modules/action.yml) stores a description of these (`base.json`) next to the archive. A job only extracts the cache of other dependencies when its description matches; otherwise it installs every dependency. Only pull requests on GitHub-hosted runners use the caches of other dependencies, as the jobs that save caches run on pushes and the other runners use another pnpm store. The caches saved on `main` therefore always come from a clean installation.

## Electron download cache

The platform jobs in [pr-node-modules.yml](../pr-node-modules.yml) also warm a
separate Electron download cache on `main`. The
[setup-electron](../../actions/setup-electron/action.yml) action shares cache
handling and download retries with the Linux, macOS, and Windows PR test
workflows:

- By default, restore cached archives and validate/prepare Electron, downloading
  with up to three attempts as needed. PR jobs use this mode without saving.
- `lookup-only: 'true'` only checks for a cache entry, without restoring archives,
  preparing Electron, or saving. This mode does not require pnpm or the
  dependencies.
- `save-cache: 'true'` also saves after successful setup on a cache miss.

The cache stores `@electron/get`'s original download archives, not the prepared
`.build/electron` application. Its key includes the runner OS, target
architecture, and a hash of `.npmrc` and `build/checksums/electron.txt`. Ordinary
`pnpm-lock.yaml` changes do not invalidate it. If a downloader update changes
the cache format, bump the `electron-download-v1` prefix in `setup-electron`.

The paths match `@electron/get`'s platform defaults, including `XDG_CACHE_HOME`
on Linux and `LOCALAPPDATA` on Windows. Cache paths and keys are handled within
the action.

Even on a cache hit, PR jobs run `pnpm run electron` to validate and prepare the
application from the cached archives using the current checkout. Checksum
validation remains enabled: the current downloader still fetches
`SHASUMS256.txt` from GitHub, so this cache avoids the large ZIP downloads but
does not make Electron setup entirely network-independent.

On `main`, an Electron cache hit uses lookup-only checks and skips downloading
Electron. On a miss, the platform job restores `node_modules` (or installs them
if that cache also misses), then invokes `setup-electron` with `save-cache: 'true'`.
This checks the cache again before preparing and saving Electron, while keeping
already-warm jobs from extracting dependency archives unnecessarily.
